A measure this long makes the eye travel too far from the end of one line to the start of the next, so readers lose their place and skim. Long lines feel efficient on a wide monitor, yet they tire the reader within a paragraph or two. Typographers have kept body text between roughly forty-five and seventy-five characters per line for centuries, and the reason is the same today: comfortable reading depends on a short return sweep. This paragraph stretches across the whole width of a large screen on purpose, so the check can see a measure far beyond that range and report it.

Leading this tight makes the ascenders of one line crowd the descenders of the line above, so the paragraph turns into a dark, even block that is hard to enter. Body text usually wants a line-height somewhere around one and a half times its size, a little more for long lines and a little less for short ones.
